faq.a: The Case tab offers UPPERCASE, lowercase, Title Case, Sentence case, aLtErNaTiNg, iNVERSE, slug-case, camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, and CONSTANT_CASE. Title Case follows the common convention of keeping minor words (a, an, the, and, of, to, in, etc.) lowercase unless they're the first or last word, and it splits on spaces rather than \w so it doesn't mangle non-Latin scripts.

Yes. Tick 'Regex' to treat the Find field as a regular expression; otherwise your search text is escaped and matched literally. There's also a 'Match case' toggle. As you type it shows a live match count, and 'Replace All' reports how many replacements were made. An invalid regex is caught and shown as an error instead of breaking the tool.

faq.q: Can I undo a transformation I didn't want?
faq.a: Yes. The tool keeps an undo history of up to 50 states, pushing a snapshot before and after each operation, so the ↩ Undo button steps back through your changes. Your text is also auto-saved to local storage (key tt_autosave) about half a second after you stop typing, so it survives a page reload.

faq.q: What cleaning and encoding operations does it include?
faq.a: The Clean tab trims spaces, removes blank lines, line breaks, special characters, numbers, HTML tags, and collapses extra spaces. The Transform tab reverses text or words, sorts/shuffles/numbers lines, removes duplicates, and adds a prefix/suffix per line. The Encode tab does URL, HTML, and Base64 encode/decode plus slugify (which also strips diacritics via NFD normalization). A live stats bar shows characters, words, sentences, paragraphs, lines, and reading time.
